run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-17T09:30:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Alert PendingPodsDetected (otel-demo) is explained by a pod-template change on two Deployments. Cluster-wide only two pods are Pending: otel-demo/ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and otel-demo/cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh; both carry PodScheduled=False with reason Unschedulable and message "0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector". Their owners are new ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 (created 2026-11-17T09:29:12Z) and cart-5b597c6db5 (created 2026-11-17T09:29:20Z), created for Deployment revision 2 of otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart, whose pod templates set nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node. The five nodes in the cluster carry hostname labels i-01a47734339426210, i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba, and only i-01a47734339426210 (control-plane) is tainted, so no node can match hostname=invalid-node and both surge pods stay unschedulable. Impact observed so far is limited: the previous revision-1 ReplicaSets (ad-554b849958, cart-755465879b, nodeSelector null) still run one ready pod each on node i-037e40963128cbd9f, and both Deployments report availableReplicas 1 for spec.replicas 1, so no capacity loss was observed; ad's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate is flat (~1.05 per 600s) from the earliest available sample 09:10 through 09:40 with no deviation at 09:29, and cart's spans in the window are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so cart's error state is unknown rather than verified clean. What applied nodeSelector=invalid-node to the two templates (Helm release otel-demo revision 2) could not be verified because change history is not integrated; a mutating webhook as the injector remains an unverified hypothesis because that query failed.

claims.text: Exactly two pods are Pending in the whole cluster, both in namespace otel-demo: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh. Both have PodScheduled=False with reason Unschedulable and message "0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.", no node assigned and empty containerStatuses.

Deployment otel-demo/ad has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"} and affinity null; it is at deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2, metadata.generation 2, status shows replicas 2, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, and Progressing reason ReplicaSetUpdated for ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975.

Deployment otel-demo/cart carries the identical fault: spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}, affinity null, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2, metadata.generation 2, status replicas 2, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, Progressing with reason ReplicaSetUpdated for ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5.

The cluster has five nodes with kubernetes.io/hostname values i-01a47734339426210, i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba; none equals "invalid-node". All five are Ready=True with allocatable cpu 4 and ~16 GiB memory, none has spec.unschedulable set, and the only taint is node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule on i-01a47734339426210.

The failing ReplicaSets were created at 09:29:12Z (ad-dd7f45975, deployment revision 2, nodeSelector invalid-node, ready/available null) and 09:29:20Z (cart-5b597c6db5, same nodeSelector), replacing the revision-1 ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and cart-755465879b, which have nodeSelector null, 1 ready and 1 available replica each. Deployment events record "Scaled up replica set ad-dd7f45975 from 0 to 1" and "Scaled up replica set cart-5b597c6db5 from 0 to 1" plus FailedScheduling warnings (count 3 each) for the two pending pods at those same times.

Deployments ad and cart are the only two workloads cluster-wide whose pod template uses "invalid-node"; the other Deployments that set a nodeSelector (ingress-nginx-controller, cilium-operator, coredns, coredns-autoscaler, ebs-csi-controller, opentelemetry-operator) use only kubernetes.io/os=linux and are available. All other otel-demo Deployments have nodeSelector null.

The superseded pods ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p are Running and Ready (restartCount 0, empty lastState) on node i-037e40963128cbd9f, so each Deployment still serves its single desired replica while the surge pod is unschedulable.

Service ad kept serving and its error level did not deviate when the pending pod appeared: STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for service_name=ad hold a flat ~1.05 per 600s window at every returned point from 09:10:00Z (earliest available sample) through 09:40:00Z, i.e. the same rate before and after the 09:29:12Z pending pod.

Service cart was still exercised during the window (increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=cart about 38902 spans over 08:30:09Z-09:44:39Z) but every returned cart series has status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no STATUS_CODE_ERROR or STATUS_CODE_OK series was returned for cart, so cart's error state is unknown rather than proven zero.

Pending is not caused by node capacity or cordoning: the scheduler message names only taint/affinity/selector mismatch (no insufficient cpu or memory clause), all five nodes are Ready with 4 CPU and ~16 GiB allocatable, and no node has spec.unschedulable set.

Deployment-level capacity for ad and cart was not lost while the surge pods were pending: both list availableReplicas 1 against spec.replicas 1, and their revision-1 pods are Running and Ready, so the two pending pods are extra rollout pods, not a serving outage.

Rejected: node resource exhaustion or insufficient allocatable CPU/memory kept the pods pending. The FailedScheduling message attributes the failure to 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector and 1 untolerated control-plane taint, and the nodes report 4 CPUs and ~16 GiB allocatable.

Rejected: a node drain or cordon or an application-node taint made the pods unschedulable. No node object has spec.unschedulable set and the only taint is node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule on node i-01a47734339426210, which the scheduler message already counts as the 1 tainted node.

Rejected: the ad service broke because its new replica could not be scheduled. The already-running revision-1 pod ad-554b849958-42mdm stayed Ready and ad's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was flat across 09:10-09:40, with no deviation at the 09:29 pending event.

A change to the Helm release "otel-demo" (release namespace otel-demo, chart opentelemetry-demo-0.38.6, revision 2 at about 09:29) set nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node on Deployments ad and cart, producing the new ReplicaSets and the two unschedulable pods. The actor and source of that value are unverified because change history is not integrated.

A mutating admission webhook could have injected the nodeSelector into the ad and cart pod templates; this remains unverified because the mutatingwebhookconfigurations query failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and no ConfigMap in the cluster was observed to contain the string invalid-node.

Remove the nodeSelector (or set kubernetes.io/hostname to a real node hostname) on Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart so the pending surge pods ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh can be scheduled and the stuck rollouts complete.

Diff the otel-demo Helm release values / GitOps source for revision 2 of the ad and cart Deployments to find where the value invalid-node was introduced, so the source is corrected rather than only the live object patched.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so what or who applied nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node to Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart at about 09:29:12Z (Helm release otel-demo revision 2) could not be verified.
The mutatingwebhookconfigurations query returned status error (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so admission-time injection of the nodeSelector can be neither confirmed nor ruled out.
The ConfigMap scan for data containing "invalid-node" returned status no_data, so it shows only that this query matched nothing; no ConfigMap-based source was identified.

Prometheus returned no series for kube_pod_status_phase or kube_deployment_status_* matching otel-demo (get_metric_names for those name patterns returned no_data), and list_prometheus_rules with rule_name PendingPodsDetected returned no_data, so the alert's exact expression and its "current: 2" value could not be confirmed from this Prometheus; the pending count was confirmed from the Kubernetes API instead.

The metrics_range_query for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count grpc status codes returned no_data, so a per-gRPC-code error breakdown for ad, cart, frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy is unknown.
traces_search_by_tags for service cart with error=true returned no_data, so no error-tagged cart trace was found; this does not prove cart spans were error-free.

Log queries on the running pods ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p for error patterns returned no_data, so they do not establish those pods are free of errors; the two pending pods produced no logs because their containers never started.
Span metric samples for ad, cart and related services begin at 09:10:00Z, so no baseline earlier than 09:10 exists for these services.
The resourcequotas query returned no_data, so quota pressure was not assessed as an alternative scheduling constraint (the scheduler message does not mention quota).
next_steps: Retrieve the otel-demo Helm release history or Git commit that produced deployment revision 2 for ad and cart and confirm the origin of the value invalid-node.
Inspect mutating admission webhook configurations (that API query failed in this Run) for anything that sets nodeSelector or tolerations on otel-demo pod templates.
After the nodeSelector is corrected, confirm the rollouts finish and that no pods remain Pending in otel-demo.
Add a CI check that fails when a pod template nodeSelector value does not match an existing node label, so this class of stuck rollout is caught before the alert.
